function_v0.doc:
Sweep genuinely-unowed SR to the treasury.

## Read this before assuming it is a revenue line \xe2\x80\x94 it usually is not
In a share-based design the surplus is **not** free money. The conservation identity is
exact: minting `sr_in` at index `i0` creates `face = sr_in \xc3\x97 i0` and leaves
`held \xe2\x88\x92 pt_cover = sr_in \xe2\x88\x92 sr_in \xc3\x97 i0/i`, which is *precisely* what YT holders are owed.
**Every stroop above PT cover belongs to some YT holder** \xe2\x80\x94 settled or not.

So this can only ever sweep what is provably owed to nobody:
* rounding remainder from the one-directional floors in the interest math, and
* claims **abandoned** by burning YT without withdrawing.

The unsettled part of holders' claims cannot be enumerated on chain, so it is bounded from
above: no holder's settlement index can be below [`storage::init_index`], so the worst-case
unsettled total is what the entire YT supply would have earned from that floor. That bound
is deliberately loose \xe2\x80\x94 a healthy series sweeps \xe2\x89\x880, which is the correct answer, not a bug.
function_v0.name: sweep_surplus

function_v0.doc:
**The mutating index \xe2\x80\x94 the number every value-MOVING path must price on.**

[`Self::py_index`] is a pure view and may lag SR by one sync. That is harmless for a quote
and wrong for a trade: `srmarket` used to price on the view while the `mint_py`/`redeem_py`
it then called internally used *this* one, so a single transaction ran on two different
indices (`FINAL_CHECK.md` V2-01). Anything that moves value calls this instead.

**Mutating**: refreshes SR from the strategy and ratchets the stored index. `sr::sync_rate`
ALWAYS writes, so the footprint stays a function of the call graph alone and cannot depend
on timing \xe2\x80\x94 the property that the 2026-08-24 testnet footprint failure taught us to keep.

Calling this and then `mint_py`/`redeem_py` in the same transaction is **consistent, not
doubled**: the ledger timestamp is fixed for the transaction, so the second sync observes
the same `b_rate` and returns the same index.
function_v0.name: py_index_current

Freeze the index at expiry. Permissionless \xe2\x80\x94 anyone may pin it, and the earlier it is

Blend exposes only the *current* rate with no historical lookup, so the expiry index cannot
be reconstructed after the fact \xe2\x80\x94 it has to be observed on chain. This is `futureamm.md`'s
"Rule A", made explicit and callable rather than left to whoever happens to touch the
contract first.
function_v0.name: stamp_expiry_index

Settle `user` and pay out their accrued SR, minus the protocol yield fee.

Returns `(paid_to_user, fee_to_treasury)`, both in SR. Callable by anyone on anyone's
behalf \xe2\x80\x94 it only ever moves value **to** the holder, so there is nothing to gate. That also
makes it safe for a keeper to sweep dust claims.
function_v0.name: redeem_due_interest

function_v0.doc: Withdraw a pending proposal. Current admin only.
function_v0.name: cancel_admin_transfer

function_v0.doc:
`redeem_due_interest`, but paying the holder's SR to `receiver` instead of to themselves.

This exists so a router can claim on the user's behalf and unwrap the proceeds to USDC in the
same transaction. Without it the router would have to claim (paying the *user*), then pull
the SR back \xe2\x80\x94 and the pull amount is only known on chain, which is exactly the
simulate-vs-execute authorization drift that bit us on testnet (`AUDITPREP.md` \xc2\xa74, item 1).

## Why the auth split is what it is

Paying a holder their own yield is safe for anyone to trigger \xe2\x80\x94 it only ever moves value
**to** them. **Redirecting** that payment is not: it moves their value to a third party. So
the permissionless case stays permissionless, and only the redirect requires the holder's
signature. Note this deliberately checks `receiver != user` rather than trusting the caller.

udt_struct_v0.doc:
A single deposit's accounting record \xe2\x80\x94 the unit that makes Spield's yield math correct.

**Per-position, never overwritten** (fixes SCF #4): every `mint` creates a *new* `Position`
with its own `entry_rate`, so topping up never clobbers an earlier tranche's entry point.

**`settled_rate` travels with the YT** (fixes SCF #5/#6): yield is always measured from
`settled_rate`, which starts at `entry_rate` and is bumped to the current rate on every
`claim_yield` *without burning YT*. A position transferred to a new owner carries its
`settled_rate`, so the buyer can only ever claim yield accrued *after* they held it.
udt_struct_v0.name: Position

fields.name: owner

fields.name: principal

fields.doc: PT still held in this position. Burned on `redeem_pt` (after maturity) and on `combine`.
fields.name: pt_amount

fields.doc: Blend `b_rate` (SCALAR_12) up to which yield has already been settled/paid. Starts equal\nto `entry_rate`; advanced to `current_rate` on each claim. Yield owed is measured from\nhere, so the same YT can be claimed across many epochs.
fields.name: settled_rate

fields.doc: Blend bToken shares this position is backed by (its slice of the wrapper's total Blend\nposition). `principal = shares * entry_rate / SCALAR_12` at mint.
fields.name: shares

fields.doc: YT still held in this position. **Never burned by `claim_yield`** \xe2\x80\x94 only by `combine`.

The bound is **time-aware**: `b_rate` may rise by at most `max_apr_bps` per year, pro-rated by
the seconds elapsed since `last_ts`. This makes the check independent of how often the strategy
is read (a long-untouched position no longer false-trips), so only `max_apr_bps` \xe2\x80\x94 calibrated
against Blend's real max borrow APR \xe2\x80\x94 needs tuning. See [`crate::math::check_rate_bound_timed`].

fields.doc: Max allowed **annual** `b_rate` growth, in basis points (e.g. `30_000` = 300% APR). Set\ngenerously above Blend's real max borrow APR so honest reads always pass.

A single Fixed-Rate Vault deposit (plan \xc2\xa711.2 / \xc2\xa77.5 \xe2\x80\x94 the flagship "lock X% fixed" product).

PT-passthrough model: the user deposits `principal` USDC and is promised exactly `payout`

vault backs every receipt with **PT it actually holds** (each PT redeems 1:1 at maturity),
